verses.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐγένετο ἀναχθῆναι ἡμᾶς ἀποσπασθέντας ἀπ’ αὐτῶν εὐθυδρομήσαντες ἤλθομεν εἰς τὴν Κῶ τῇ δὲ ἑξῆς εἰς τὴν Ῥόδον κἀκεῖθεν εἰς Πάταρα
verses.transliteration: Hōs de egeneto anachthēnai hēmas apospasthentas ap’ autōn euthydromēsantes ēlthomen eis tēn Kō tē de hexēs eis tēn Rhodon kakeithen eis Patara
verses.literal: After we had torn ourselves away from them we sailed directly . . . to Cos and the next day on to Rhodes and from there to Patara
verses.literalPt: Depois de nos apartarmos deles, fizemo-nos à vela, e, indo em direitura, chegamos a Cós, no dia seguinte, a Rodes, e, dali, a Pátara;

verses.original: καὶ εὑρόντες πλοῖον διαπερῶν εἰς Φοινίκην ἐπιβάντες ἀνήχθημεν
verses.transliteration: kai heurontes ploion diaperōn eis Phoinikēn epibantes anēchthēmen
verses.literal: Finding a ship crossing over to Phoenicia we boarded it and set sail
verses.literalPt: e, tendo encontrado um navio que passava para Fenícia, embarcando nele, seguimos viagem.

verses.original: ἀναφάναντες δὲ τὴν Κύπρον καὶ καταλιπόντες αὐτὴν εὐώνυμον ἐπλέομεν εἰς Συρίαν καὶ κατήλθομεν εἰς Τύρον ἐκεῖσε γὰρ τὸ πλοῖον ἦν ἀποφορτιζόμενον τὸν γόμον
verses.transliteration: anaphanantes de tēn Kypron kai katalipontes autēn euōnymon epleomen eis Syrian kai katēlthomen eis Tyron ekeise gar to ploion ēn apophortizomenon ton gomon
verses.literal: After sighting Cyprus and passing south of it . . . . . . we sailed on to Syria and landed at Tyre where the ship was to unload its cargo
verses.literalPt: Tendo avistado a Chipre, deixando-a à esquerda, navegamos para a Síria e desembarcamos em Tiro; pois aí se devia descarregar o navio.

verses.original: Ἀνευρόντες δὲ τοὺς μαθητὰς ἐπεμείναμεν αὐτοῦ ἡμέρας ἑπτά οἵτινες τῷ Παύλῳ ἔλεγον διὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος μὴ ἐπιβαίνειν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα
verses.transliteration: Aneurontes de tous mathētas epemeinamen autou hēmeras hepta hoitines tō Paulō elegon dia tou Pneumatos mē epibainein eis Hierosolyma
verses.literal: We sought out the disciples in Tyre and stayed with them seven days Through the Spirit they kept telling Paul not to go up to Jerusalem
verses.literalPt: Tendo achado os discípulos, permanecemos aí sete dias; e eles, pelo Espírito, diziam a Paulo que não entrasse em Jerusalém.

verses.original: ὅτε δὲ ἐγένετο ἐξαρτίσαι ἡμᾶς τὰς ἡμέρας ἐξελθόντες ἐπορευόμεθα προπεμπόντων ἡμᾶς πάντων σὺν γυναιξὶ καὶ τέκνοις ἕως ἔξω τῆς πόλεως καὶ θέντες τὰ γόνατα ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν προσευξάμενοι
verses.transliteration: hote de egeneto exartisai hēmas tas hēmeras exelthontes eporeuometha propempontōn hēmas pantōn syn gynaixi kai teknois heōs exō tēs poleōs kai thentes ta gonata epi ton aigialon proseuxamenoi
verses.literal: But when our time there had ended we set out on our journey All the disciples with their wives and children accompanied us out of the city and knelt down . . . . . . on the beach to pray with us
verses.literalPt: Quando findaram esses dias, partimos e seguimos a nossa viagem, acompanhados por todos, com suas mulheres e filhos, até fora da cidade; ajoelhados na praia, oramos e, despedindo-nos uns dos outros,

verses.original: ἀπησπασάμεθα ἀλλήλους καὶ ἐνέβημεν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον ἐκεῖνοι δὲ ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς τὰ ἴδια
verses.transliteration: apēspasametha allēlous kai enebēmen eis to ploion ekeinoi de hypestrepsan eis ta idia
verses.literal: And after we had said our farewells . . . we went aboard . . . the ship and they returned home
verses.literalPt: embarcamos, e eles voltaram para suas casas.

verses.original: Ἡμεῖς δὲ τὸν πλοῦν διανύσαντες ἀπὸ Τύρου κατηντήσαμεν εἰς Πτολεμαΐδα καὶ ἀσπασάμενοι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ἐμείναμεν ἡμέραν μίαν παρ’ αὐτοῖς
verses.transliteration: Hēmeis de ton ploun dianysantes apo Tyrou katēntēsamen eis Ptolemaida kai aspasamenoi tous adelphous emeinamen hēmeran mian par’ autois
verses.literal: When we had finished our voyage from Tyre we landed at Ptolemais where we greeted the brothers and stayed with them for a day
verses.literalPt: Concluída a viagem de Tiro, chegamos a Ptolemaida; depois de saudarmos os irmãos, passamos um dia com eles.

verses.original: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον ἐξελθόντες ἤλθομεν εἰς Καισάρειαν καὶ εἰσελθόντες εἰς τὸν οἶκον Φιλίππου τοῦ εὐαγγελιστοῦ ὄντος ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ ἐμείναμεν παρ’ αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: Tē de epaurion exelthontes ēlthomen eis Kaisareian kai eiselthontes eis ton oikon Philippou tou euangelistou ontos ek tōn hepta emeinamen par’ autō
verses.literal: Leaving the next day we went on to Caesarea and stayed - at the home of Philip the evangelist who was one of the Seven
verses.literalPt: Partindo no dia seguinte, fomos a Cesareia; e, entrando na casa de Filipe, o evangelista, que era um dos sete, ficamos com ele.

verses.original: τούτῳ δὲ ἦσαν θυγατέρες τέσσαρες παρθένοι προφητεύουσαι
verses.transliteration: toutō de ēsan thygateres tessares parthenoi prophēteuousai
verses.literal: He had four unmarried daughters who prophesied
verses.literalPt: Este tinha quatro filhas virgens, que profetizavam.

verses.original: Ἐπιμενόντων δὲ ἡμέρας πλείους κατῆλθέν τις ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας προφήτης ὀνόματι Ἅγαβος
verses.transliteration: Epimenontōn de hēmeras pleious katēlthen tis apo tēs Ioudaias prophētēs onomati Hagabos
verses.literal: After we had been there several days a prophet named Agabus came down from Judea
verses.literalPt: Demorando-nos ali por muitos dias, desceu da Judeia um profeta chamado Ágabo,

verses.original: καὶ ἐλθὼν πρὸς ἡμᾶς καὶ ἄρας τὴν ζώνην τοῦ Παύλου δήσας ἑαυτοῦ τοὺς πόδας καὶ τὰς χεῖρας εἶπεν Τάδε λέγει τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον Τὸν ἄνδρα οὗ ἐστιν ἡ ζώνη αὕτη οὕτως δήσουσιν ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ παραδώσουσιν εἰς χεῖρας ἐθνῶν
verses.transliteration: kai elthōn pros hēmas kai aras tēn zōnēn tou Paulou dēsas heautou tous podas kai tas cheiras eipen Tade legei to Pneuma to Hagion Ton andra hou estin hē zōnē hautē houtōs dēsousin en Ierousalēm hoi Ioudaioi kai paradōsousin eis cheiras ethnōn
verses.literal: Coming over to us he took Paul’s belt bound his own feet and hands and said The Holy Spirit says In this way the Jews of Jerusalem will bind the owner of . . . . . . this belt and hand him over . . . . . . to the Gentiles
verses.literalPt: e, vindo ter conosco, tomou a cinta de Paulo, ligou com ela os seus próprios pés e mãos e disse: Isto diz o Espírito Santo: Assim os judeus, em Jerusalém, ligarão o homem a quem pertence esta cinta e o entregarão nas mãos dos gentios.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ ἠκούσαμεν ταῦτα παρεκαλοῦμεν ἡμεῖς τε καὶ οἱ ἐντόπιοι τοῦ μὴ ἀναβαίνειν αὐτὸν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ
verses.transliteration: hōs de ēkousamen tauta parekaloumen hēmeis te kai hoi entopioi tou mē anabainein auton eis Ierousalēm
verses.literal: When we heard this we and the people there pleaded with Paul not to go up to Jerusalem
verses.literalPt: Quando ouvimos isso, nós e os daquele lugar rogamos a Paulo que não subisse a Jerusalém.

verses.original: Τότε ἀπεκρίθη ὁ Παῦλος Τί ποιεῖτε κλαίοντες καὶ συνθρύπτοντές μου τὴν καρδίαν ἐγὼ γὰρ οὐ μόνον δεθῆναι ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀποθανεῖν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἑτοίμως ἔχω ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ
verses.transliteration: Tote apekrithē ho Paulos Ti poieite klaiontes kai synthryptontes mou tēn kardian egō gar ou monon dethēnai alla kai apothanein eis Ierousalēm hetoimōs echō hyper tou onomatos tou Kyriou Iēsou
verses.literal: Then Paul answered Why are you weeping and breaking my heart I am ready not only to be bound but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus
verses.literalPt: Então, ele respondeu: Que fazeis chorando e magoando-me o coração? Pois eu estou pronto não só para ser ligado, mas até para morrer em Jerusalém pelo nome do Senhor Jesus.

verses.original: μὴ πειθομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ ἡσυχάσαμεν εἰπόντες Τοῦ Κυρίου τὸ θέλημα γινέσθω
verses.transliteration: mē peithomenou de autou hēsychasamen eipontes Tou Kyriou to thelēma ginesthō
verses.literal: When he would not be dissuaded we quieted down and said The Lord’s will be done
verses.literalPt: Como não pudéssemos persuadi-lo, desistimos, dizendo: Faça-se a vontade do Senhor!

verses.original: Μετὰ δὲ τὰς ἡμέρας ταύτας ἐπισκευασάμενοι ἀνεβαίνομεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα
verses.transliteration: Meta de tas hēmeras tautas episkeuasamenoi anebainomen eis Hierosolyma
verses.literal: After these days we packed up and went on to Jerusalem
verses.literalPt: Depois desses dias, tendo feito os preparativos, subimos a Jerusalém;

verses.original: συνῆλθον δὲ καὶ τῶν μαθητῶν ἀπὸ Καισαρείας σὺν ἡμῖν ἄγοντες παρ’ ᾧ ξενισθῶμεν Μνάσωνί τινι Κυπρίῳ ἀρχαίῳ μαθητῇ
verses.transliteration: synēlthon de kai tōn mathētōn apo Kaisareias syn hēmin agontes par’ hō xenisthōmen Mnasōni tini Kypriō archaiō mathētē
verses.literal: Some of the disciples from Caesarea accompanied . . . us and they took us to stay at the home of Mnason the Cypriot an early disciple
verses.literalPt: e alguns discípulos foram também conosco de Cesareia, levando consigo um certo Mnasom, de Chipre, discípulo antigo, com quem nos deveríamos hospedar.

verses.original: Γενομένων δὲ ἡμῶν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἀσμένως ἀπεδέξαντο ἡμᾶς οἱ ἀδελφοί
verses.transliteration: Genomenōn de hēmōn eis Hierosolyma asmenōs apedexanto hēmas hoi adelphoi
verses.literal: When we arrived in Jerusalem the brothers welcomed us joyfully
verses.literalPt: Tendo nós chegado a Jerusalém, os irmãos nos receberam alegremente.

verses.original: τῇ δὲ ἐπιούσῃ εἰσῄει ὁ Παῦλος σὺν ἡμῖν πρὸς Ἰάκωβον πάντες τε παρεγένοντο οἱ πρεσβύτεροι
verses.transliteration: tē de epiousē eisēei ho Paulos syn hēmin pros Iakōbon pantes te paregenonto hoi presbyteroi
verses.literal: The next day Paul went in with us to see James and all the elders were present
verses.literalPt: No dia seguinte, Paulo foi, em nossa companhia, ter com Tiago; e estavam presentes todos os presbíteros.

verses.original: καὶ ἀσπασάμενος αὐτοὺς ἐξηγεῖτο καθ’ ἓν ἕκαστον ὧν ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεὸς ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν διὰ τῆς διακονίας αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: kai aspasamenos autous exēgeito kath’ hen hekaston hōn epoiēsen ho Theos en tois ethnesin dia tēs diakonias autou
verses.literal: Paul greeted them and recounted one by one the things that God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry
verses.literalPt: Paulo, tendo-os saudado, contou uma por uma as coisas que Deus fizera entre os gentios pelo seu ministério.

verses.original: Οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες ἐδόξαζον τὸν Θεόν εἶπόν τε αὐτῷ Θεωρεῖς ἀδελφέ πόσαι μυριάδες εἰσὶν ἐν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις τῶν πεπιστευκότων καὶ πάντες ζηλωταὶ τοῦ νόμου ὑπάρχουσιν
verses.transliteration: Hoi de akousantes edoxazon ton Theon eipon te autō Theōreis adelphe posai myriades eisin en tois Ioudaiois tōn pepisteukotōn kai pantes zēlōtai tou nomou hyparchousin
verses.literal: When they heard this they glorified God Then they said to Paul You see brother how many thousands of Jews have believed and all of them are zealous for the law
verses.literalPt: Eles, depois de o ouvir, glorificaram a Deus e disseram-lhe: Bem vês, irmão, quantos milhares há que têm crido entre os judeus; e todos são zelosos da Lei

verses.original: κατηχήθησαν δὲ περὶ σοῦ ὅτι ἀποστασίαν διδάσκεις ἀπὸ Μωϋσέως τοὺς κατὰ τὰ ἔθνη πάντας Ἰουδαίους λέγων μὴ περιτέμνειν αὐτοὺς τὰ τέκνα μηδὲ τοῖς ἔθεσιν περιπατεῖν
verses.transliteration: katēchēthēsan de peri sou hoti apostasian didaskeis apo Mōuseōs tous kata ta ethnē pantas Ioudaious legōn mē peritemnein autous ta tekna mēde tois ethesin peripatein
verses.literal: But they are under the impression . . . that you teach all the Jews who live among the Gentiles to forsake . . . Moses telling them not to circumcise their children or observe . . . our customs
verses.literalPt: e têm sido informados a teu respeito de que ensinas todos os judeus que estão entre os gentios a apostatarem de Moisés, dizendo-lhes que não circuncidem seus filhos, nem andem segundo os nossos ritos.

verses.original: τί οὖν ἐστιν πάντως ἀκούσονται ὅτι ἐλήλυθας
verses.transliteration: ti oun estin pantōs akousontai hoti elēlythas
verses.literal: What then should we do They will certainly hear that you have come
verses.literalPt: Que se há de fazer, pois? Certamente, saberão que tu és chegado.

verses.original: Τοῦτο οὖν ποίησον ὅ σοι λέγομεν εἰσὶν ἡμῖν ἄνδρες τέσσαρες εὐχὴν ἔχοντες ἐφ’ ἑαυτῶν
verses.transliteration: Touto oun poiēson ho soi legomen eisin hēmin andres tessares euchēn echontes eph’ heautōn
verses.literal: Therefore do what we advise you There are four men with us who have taken a vow
verses.literalPt: Faze, pois, isto que te vamos dizer: temos quatro homens que fizeram voto;

verses.original: τούτους παραλαβὼν ἁγνίσθητι σὺν αὐτοῖς καὶ δαπάνησον ἐπ’ αὐτοῖς ἵνα ξυρήσονται τὴν κεφαλήν καὶ γνώσονται πάντες ὅτι ὧν κατήχηνται περὶ σοῦ οὐδέν ἐστιν ἀλλὰ στοιχεῖς καὶ αὐτὸς φυλάσσων τὸν νόμον
verses.transliteration: toutous paralabōn hagnisthēti syn autois kai dapanēson ep’ autois hina xyrēsontai tēn kephalēn kai gnōsontai pantes hoti hōn katēchēntai peri sou ouden estin alla stoicheis kai autos phylassōn ton nomon
verses.literal: Take these men purify yourself along with them and pay their expenses . . . . . . so they can have their heads shaved Then everyone will know that there is no truth to these rumors about you but that you also live in obedience to the law
verses.literalPt: toma-os, purifica-te com eles e faze a despesa necessária para raparem a cabeça; e saberão todos que não é verdade aquilo de que têm sido informados a teu respeito, mas que andas também retamente, guardando a Lei.

verses.original: Περὶ δὲ τῶν πεπιστευκότων ἐθνῶν ἡμεῖς ἐπεστείλαμεν κρίναντες φυλάσσεσθαι αὐτοὺς τό τε εἰδωλόθυτον καὶ αἷμα καὶ πνικτὸν καὶ πορνείαν
verses.transliteration: Peri de tōn pepisteukotōn ethnōn hēmeis epesteilamen krinantes phylassesthai autous to te eidōlothyton kai haima kai pnikton kai porneian
verses.literal: As for the Gentile believers we have written to them our decision that they must abstain from food sacrificed to idols from blood from the meat of strangled animals and from sexual immorality
verses.literalPt: Mas, quanto aos gentios que têm crido, já escrevemos, ordenando que se abstenham do que é sacrificado aos ídolos, de sangue, de animais sufocados e de fornicação.

verses.original: Τότε ὁ Παῦλος παραλαβὼν τοὺς ἄνδρας τῇ ἐχομένῃ ἡμέρᾳ σὺν αὐτοῖς ἁγνισθεὶς εἰσῄει εἰς τὸ ἱερόν διαγγέλλων τὴν ἐκπλήρωσιν τῶν ἡμερῶν τοῦ ἁγνισμοῦ ἕως οὗ προσηνέχθη ὑπὲρ ἑνὸς ἑκάστου αὐτῶν ἡ προσφορά
verses.transliteration: Tote ho Paulos paralabōn tous andras tē echomenē hēmera syn autois hagnistheis eisēei eis to hieron diangellōn tēn ekplērōsin tōn hēmerōn tou hagnismou heōs hou prosēnechthē hyper henos hekastou autōn hē prosphora
verses.literal: So the next day Paul took the men and purified himself along with them Then he entered . . . the temple to give notice of the date when their purification would be complete and the offering would be made for each . . . of them
verses.literalPt: Então, Paulo, tomando aqueles homens, no dia seguinte, purificou-se com eles e entrou no templo, notificando o cumprimento dos dias da purificação em que cada um deles deveria trazer a oferenda.

verses.original: Ὡς δὲ ἔμελλον αἱ ἑπτὰ ἡμέραι συντελεῖσθαι οἱ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἀσίας Ἰουδαῖοι θεασάμενοι αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ συνέχεον πάντα τὸν ὄχλον καὶ ἐπέβαλον ἐπ’ αὐτὸν τὰς χεῖρας
verses.transliteration: Hōs de emellon hai hepta hēmerai synteleisthai hoi apo tēs Asias Ioudaioi theasamenoi auton en tō hierō synecheon panta ton ochlon kai epebalon ep’ auton tas cheiras
verses.literal: When the seven days were almost over some Jews from the province of Asia saw Paul at the temple They stirred up the whole crowd and seized . . . . . . . . . him
verses.literalPt: Mas, quando os sete dias estavam findando, os judeus vindos da Ásia, tendo visto Paulo no templo, alvoroçaram todo o povo e agarraram-no,

verses.original: κράζοντες Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται βοηθεῖτε οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ κατὰ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ τοῦ νόμου καὶ τοῦ τόπου τούτου πάντας πανταχῇ διδάσκων ἔτι τε καὶ Ἕλληνας εἰσήγαγεν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ κεκοίνωκεν τὸν ἅγιον τόπον τοῦτον
verses.transliteration: krazontes Andres Israēlitai boētheite houtos estin ho anthrōpos ho kata tou laou kai tou nomou kai tou topou toutou pantas pantachē didaskōn eti te kai Hellēnas eisēgagen eis to hieron kai kekoinōken ton hagion topon touton
verses.literal: crying out Men of Israel help us This is the man who teaches everyone everywhere against our people and against our law and against this place Furthermore . . . . . . he has brought Greeks into the temple and defiled this holy place
verses.literalPt: gritando: Israelitas, acudi! Este é o homem que por toda parte prega a todos contra o povo, contra a Lei e contra esse lugar; e, além disso, introduziu gregos no templo e tem profanado este lugar santo.

verses.original: ἦσαν γὰρ προεωρακότες Τρόφιμον τὸν Ἐφέσιον ἐν τῇ πόλει σὺν αὐτῷ ὃν ἐνόμιζον ὅτι εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν εἰσήγαγεν ὁ Παῦλος
verses.transliteration: ēsan gar proeōrakotes Trophimon ton Ephesion en tē polei syn autō hon enomizon hoti eis to hieron eisēgagen ho Paulos
verses.literal: For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city and they assumed that Paul had brought him into the temple
verses.literalPt: Pois, antes, tinham visto com ele na cidade Trófimo, de Éfeso, e julgavam que Paulo o introduzira no templo.

verses.original: Ἐκινήθη τε ἡ πόλις ὅλη καὶ ἐγένετο συνδρομὴ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ ἐπιλαβόμενοι τοῦ Παύλου εἷλκον αὐτὸν ἔξω τοῦ ἱεροῦ καὶ εὐθέως ἐκλείσθησαν αἱ θύραι
verses.transliteration: Ekinēthē te hē polis holē kai egeneto syndromē tou laou kai epilabomenoi tou Paulou heilkon auton exō tou hierou kai eutheōs ekleisthēsan hai thyrai
verses.literal: The whole city was stirred up and the people rushed together They seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple and at once the gates were shut
verses.literalPt: Alvoroçou-se toda a cidade, e houve ajuntamento do povo; e, agarrando a Paulo, arrastaram-no para fora do templo; e imediatamente foram fechadas as portas.

verses.original: Ζητούντων τε αὐτὸν ἀποκτεῖναι ἀνέβη φάσις τῷ χιλιάρχῳ τῆς σπείρης ὅτι ὅλη συνχύννεται Ἰερουσαλήμ
verses.transliteration: Zētountōn te auton apokteinai anebē phasis tō chiliarchō tēs speirēs hoti holē synchynnetai Ierousalēm
verses.literal: While they were trying to kill him the commander of the Roman regiment received a report that all Jerusalem was in turmoil
verses.literalPt: Procurando eles matá-lo, o tribuno da coorte foi avisado de que toda a Jerusalém estava amotinada;

verses.original: ὃς ἐξαυτῆς παραλαβὼν στρατιώτας καὶ ἑκατοντάρχας κατέδραμεν ἐπ’ αὐτούς οἱ δὲ ἰδόντες τὸν χιλίαρχον καὶ τοὺς στρατιώτας ἐπαύσαντο τύπτοντες τὸν Παῦλον
verses.transliteration: hos exautēs paralabōn stratiōtas kai hekatontarchas katedramen ep’ autous hoi de idontes ton chiliarchon kai tous stratiōtas epausanto typtontes ton Paulon
verses.literal: Immediately he took some soldiers and centurions and ran down to the crowd - When the people saw the commander and the soldiers they stopped beating Paul
verses.literalPt: e este, levando logo soldados e centuriões consigo, correu a eles, os quais, tendo visto ao tribuno e aos soldados, cessaram de espancar a Paulo.

verses.original: Τότε ἐγγίσας ὁ χιλίαρχος ἐπελάβετο αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκέλευσεν δεθῆναι ἁλύσεσι δυσί καὶ ἐπυνθάνετο τίς εἴη καὶ τί ἐστιν πεποιηκώς
verses.transliteration: Tote engisas ho chiliarchos epelabeto autou kai ekeleusen dethēnai halysesi dysi kai epynthaneto tis eiē kai ti estin pepoiēkōs
verses.literal: The commander came up and arrested Paul ordering that he be bound with two chains Then he asked who he was and what he had done
verses.literalPt: Então, chegando-se o tribuno, prendeu-o, e ordenou que fosse acorrentado com duas cadeias, e perguntou-lhe quem era e o que tinha feito.

verses.original: Ἄλλοι δὲ ἄλλο τι ἐπεφώνουν ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ μὴ δυναμένου δὲ αὐτοῦ γνῶναι τὸ ἀσφαλὲς διὰ τὸν θόρυβον ἐκέλευσεν ἄγεσθαι αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν
verses.transliteration: Alloi de allo ti epephōnoun en tō ochlō mē dynamenou de autou gnōnai to asphales dia ton thorybon ekeleusen agesthai auton eis tēn parembolēn
verses.literal: Some in the crowd were shouting one thing and some another And since the commander could not get at the truth because of the uproar he ordered that Paul be brought into the barracks
verses.literalPt: Na multidão uns gritavam de um modo; outros, de outro; e, não podendo, por causa do tumulto, saber a verdade, mandou que Paulo fosse recolhido à cidadela.

verses.original: ὅτε δὲ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀναβαθμούς συνέβη βαστάζεσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν στρατιωτῶν διὰ τὴν βίαν τοῦ ὄχλου
verses.transliteration: hote de egeneto epi tous anabathmous synebē bastazesthai auton hypo tōn stratiōtōn dia tēn bian tou ochlou
verses.literal: When Paul reached . . . the steps he had to be carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the mob
verses.literalPt: Ao chegar às escadas, foi ele carregado pelos soldados por causa da violência do povo;

verses.original: ἠκολούθει γὰρ τὸ πλῆθος τοῦ λαοῦ κράζοντες Αἶρε αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: ēkolouthei gar to plēthos tou laou krazontes Aire auton
verses.literal: For the crowd . . . . . . that followed him kept shouting Away with him
verses.literalPt: pois a multidão o seguia, gritando: Mata-o!

verses.original: Μέλλων τε εἰσάγεσθαι εἰς τὴν παρεμβολὴν ὁ Παῦλος λέγει τῷ χιλιάρχῳ Εἰ ἔξεστίν μοι εἰπεῖν τι πρὸς σέ Ὁ δὲ ἔφη Ἑλληνιστὶ γινώσκεις
verses.transliteration: Mellōn te eisagesthai eis tēn parembolēn ho Paulos legei tō chiliarchō Ei exestin moi eipein ti pros se Ho de ephē Hellēnisti ginōskeis
verses.literal: As they were about to take Paul into the barracks he asked the commander May I say something to you Do you speak Greek he replied
verses.literalPt: Quando Paulo estava para ser recolhido à cidadela, perguntou ao tribuno: É-me permitido dizer-te alguma coisa? Respondeu ele: Sabes grego?

verses.original: οὐκ ἄρα σὺ εἶ ὁ Αἰγύπτιος ὁ πρὸ τούτων τῶν ἡμερῶν ἀναστατώσας καὶ ἐξαγαγὼν εἰς τὴν ἔρημον τοὺς τετρακισχιλίους ἄνδρας τῶν Σικαρίων
verses.transliteration: ouk ara sy ei ho Aigyptios ho pro toutōn tōn hēmerōn anastatōsas kai exagagōn eis tēn erēmon tous tetrakischilious andras tōn Sikariōn
verses.literal: Aren’t . . . you the Egyptian who incited a rebellion some time ago . . . . . . . . . and led four thousand members of the Assassins into the wilderness
verses.literalPt: Porventura, não és tu o egípcio que há tempos sublevou e conduziu ao deserto os quatro mil sicários?

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Παῦλος Ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπος μέν εἰμι Ἰουδαῖος Ταρσεὺς τῆς Κιλικίας οὐκ ἀσήμου πόλεως πολίτης δέομαι δέ σου ἐπίτρεψόν μοι λαλῆσαι πρὸς τὸν λαόν
verses.transliteration: Eipen de ho Paulos Egō anthrōpos men eimi Ioudaios Tarseus tēs Kilikias ouk asēmou poleōs politēs deomai de sou epitrepson moi lalēsai pros ton laon
verses.literal: But Paul answered I am a Jew . . . from Tarsus in Cilicia a citizen of no ordinary city Now I beg you to allow me to speak to the people
verses.literalPt: Paulo, porém, replicou: Eu sou judeu, cidadão de Tarso, cidade não insignificante da Cilícia; e rogo-te que me permitas falar ao povo.

verses.original: ἐπιτρέψαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος ἑστὼς ἐπὶ τῶν ἀναβαθμῶν κατέσεισεν τῇ χειρὶ τῷ λαῷ πολλῆς δὲ σιγῆς γενομένης προσεφώνησεν τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ λέγων
verses.transliteration: epitrepsantos de autou ho Paulos hestōs epi tōn anabathmōn kateseisen tē cheiri tō laō pollēs de sigēs genomenēs prosephōnēsen tē Hebraidi dialektō legōn
verses.literal: Having received permission Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the crowd - A great hush came over the crowd and he addressed them in Hebrew . . . . . .
verses.literalPt: Tendo-lho permitido, Paulo, em pé na escada, fez sinal ao povo com a mão; e, feito um grande silêncio, falou em língua hebraica, dizendo:
